words.enDefinition: To arrange for a restaurant to hold a table for you

examples.en: We agreed to book a table for the evening after our final exam.
examples.zh: 我们商量好「预订餐桌」，在最后一门课考完的那天晚上去吃饭。

examples.en: My roommate offered to book a table near the theater before the show.
examples.zh: 室友提出演出前在剧院附近「预订餐桌」。

words.enDefinition: A restaurant table intended for two people to sit at

examples.en: I asked for a table for two when my friend arrived from campus.
examples.zh: 朋友从学校过来后，我问有没有「两人桌」。

examples.en: The host showed us to a table for two near the back wall.
examples.zh: 迎宾员领我们到了靠近后墙的一张「两人桌」。

collocations: ask for a table for two
a table for two by the window

words.enDefinition: A group of four people dining together at a restaurant

examples.en: The host asked whether our whole party of four had arrived at the café.
examples.zh: 迎宾员问我们「四位客人」是不是都到咖啡馆了。

examples.en: My roommate said we were a party of four and gave our names.
examples.zh: 室友说我们有「四位客人」，还报了姓名。

collocations: a reservation for a party of four
room for a party of four

words.enDefinition: The name used to identify a reserved table in restaurant records

examples.en: The host asked me for the name on the reservation before checking the tablet.
examples.zh: 迎宾员问我「订位登记姓名」是什么，然后查了平板。

examples.en: I gave my friend the name on the reservation in case she arrived first.
examples.zh: 我把「订位登记姓名」告诉朋友，免得她先到时不知道报什么名字。

collocations: check the name on the reservation
give the name on the reservation
confirm the name on the reservation

words.zhGloss: 我们的订位登记在某人名下
words.enDefinition: A phrase introducing the name used for an existing reservation
acceptedZhAnswers: 我们的订位登记在某人名下

examples.en: I told the host, "We have a reservation under my roommate’s name," and showed the email.
examples.zh: 我跟迎宾员说「我们的订位登记在室友名下」，然后出示了邮件。

examples.en: The message says "We have a reservation under Lee," so tell the host that name.
examples.zh: 消息里说「我们的订位登记在李的名下」，所以到店后请报这个姓名。

collocations: we have a reservation under Chen
we have a reservation under my name
we have a reservation under my friend's name

words.enDefinition: A message verifying that a restaurant has saved a table

examples.en: The reservation confirmation showed the time and the address of the restaurant.
examples.zh: 「订位确认信息」上写了时间和餐厅地址。

examples.en: I forwarded the reservation confirmation to the friend who was meeting us.
examples.zh: 我把「订位确认信息」转发给了来和我们碰面的朋友。

words.enDefinition: To alter details of a booking already made with a restaurant

examples.en: I called to change a reservation after another classmate decided to join us.
examples.zh: 又有一位同学决定加入之后，我打电话「修改订位」。

examples.en: The host told me whom to contact to change a reservation for tonight.
examples.zh: 迎宾员告诉我，今晚的餐要找谁「修改订位」。

words.enDefinition: A diner who arrives without booking a table in advance

examples.en: The host gave a walk-in guest the next available table for one.
examples.zh: 迎宾员把下一张空出的一人桌安排给了一位「没订位就到店的客人」。

examples.en: I asked whether a walk-in guest could sit at the counter instead.
examples.zh: 我问「没订位就到店的客人」可不可以改坐吧台。

words.zhGloss: 你们接待没订位的客人吗
words.enDefinition: A question asking whether customers can enter without reserving a table
acceptedZhAnswers: 你们接待没订位的客人吗

examples.en: I called the café and asked, "Do you take walk-ins?" before walking over.
examples.zh: 我走过去之前先给咖啡馆打了电话，问「你们接待没订位的客人吗？」

examples.en: My friend asked, "Do you take walk-ins?" when we reached the restaurant near campus.
examples.zh: 我们找到学校附近的那家餐厅时，朋友问「你们接待没订位的客人吗？」

collocations: say "Do you take walk-ins on weekends?"
ask "Do you take walk-ins at lunch?"

words.expression: put your name on the list
words.lemma: put your name on the list
words.zhGloss: 把姓名登记到等位名单
words.enDefinition: To record your name among people waiting to be seated
acceptedZhAnswers: 把姓名登记到等位名单
acceptedEnVariants: put your name on the list

examples.en: The host asked if she could "Put your name on the list" before we waited outside.
examples.zh: 迎宾员问能不能先「把姓名登记到等位名单」，再请我们到外面等。

examples.en: The sign asks you to put your name on the list before choosing a seat.
examples.zh: 牌子提示，选座之前要先「把姓名登记到等位名单」。

collocations: ask to put your name on the list
offer to put your name on the list
put your name on the list first

words.enDefinition: The approximate amount of time before a table may become available

examples.en: The estimated wait was shorter for a table by the entrance.
examples.zh: 入口旁的桌子「预计等候时间」比较短。

examples.en: I repeated the estimated wait to my friends waiting outside the café.
examples.zh: 我把「预计等候时间」告诉了正在咖啡馆外等的朋友。

words.enDefinition: The station where restaurant staff greet guests and assign seating

examples.en: The host stand was just inside the entrance on our left.
examples.zh: 「迎宾台」就在入口进去左手边。

examples.en: I left our reservation details with the person at the host stand.
examples.zh: 我把订位信息留给了「迎宾台」的店员。

collocations: check in at the host stand

words.enDefinition: A sign politely asking diners to wait for seating assistance

examples.en: The sign said "Please wait to be seated," so we stayed beside the entrance.
examples.zh: 牌子上写着「请等候店员安排座位」，我们就留在入口旁边。

examples.en: I noticed "Please wait to be seated" on the door before our group went inside.
examples.zh: 我们一行人进门前，我注意到门口写着「请等候店员安排座位」。

collocations: a "Please wait to be seated" sign
see "Please wait to be seated" at the entrance

words.enDefinition: To choose an available table without waiting for staff to assign one

examples.en: The sign said "Seat yourself," so we sat in the corner.
examples.zh: 牌子上写着「请自行入座」，我们就在角落坐下了。

examples.en: I asked what "Seat yourself" meant before walking past the entrance.
examples.zh: 进门之前，我问了「请自行入座」是什么意思。

collocations: a sign saying to seat yourself
ask if you can seat yourself

words.enDefinition: To guide you to the table assigned to you

examples.en: The host said, "A colleague will show you to your table in a moment."
examples.zh: 迎宾员说，马上会有同事「领你们到座位」。

examples.en: The host told my friend, "I can show you to your table by the window."
examples.zh: 迎宾员跟我朋友说，可以「领你到靠窗的座位」。

collocations: come to show you to your table
ready to show you to your table
wait to show you to your table

words.enDefinition: A table that is open for customers to sit at

examples.en: We asked about an available table because our lecture had ended early.
examples.zh: 我们的课提前结束了，就问餐厅有没有「空桌」。

examples.en: The host saw an available table behind the group waiting for dessert.
examples.zh: 迎宾员发现，等甜点的那群客人身后有一张「空桌」。

collocations: an available table near the door

words.enDefinition: A restaurant table placed near a window

examples.en: We chose a window table because we wanted to watch the rain.
examples.zh: 我们选了张「靠窗的餐桌」，想看看外头下雨。

examples.en: The host said a window table would be available after the lunch rush.
examples.zh: 迎宾员说午餐高峰过后会有一张「靠窗的餐桌」空出来。

words.enDefinition: Restaurant seating with fixed benches around or alongside a table

examples.en: We chose booth seating because it gave us more space for our bags.
examples.zh: 我们选了「卡座座位」，因为能腾出更多地方放包。

examples.en: The café had booth seating along one wall and stools near the window.
examples.zh: 咖啡馆沿一侧墙摆了「卡座座位」，靠窗放的是凳子。

words.enDefinition: Tables and chairs set outside for diners to use

examples.en: We asked about outdoor seating because the air inside was quite warm.
examples.zh: 店里有点热，我们就问有没有「户外座位」。

examples.en: The restaurant opened its outdoor seating when the rain stopped before lunch.
examples.zh: 午饭前雨停了，餐厅便开放了「户外座位」。

words.enDefinition: A dining table on a patio outside the main building

examples.en: The server brought menus to our patio table near the planters.
examples.zh: 服务员把菜单拿到我们靠近花盆的「露台餐桌」上。

examples.en: My friend moved her chair closer to the patio table to make room.
examples.zh: 朋友把椅子往「露台餐桌」拉近一些，好让出地方。

words.enDefinition: Places for diners to sit directly along a restaurant counter

examples.en: We chose counter seating because we could see the kitchen from there.
examples.zh: 我们选了「吧台座位」，因为那里能看到厨房。

examples.en: The café had counter seating but only two tables for larger groups.
examples.zh: 咖啡馆有「吧台座位」，但能坐较多人的桌子只有两张。

words.enDefinition: A large eating table shared by people from different groups

examples.en: We found two empty seats at the communal table in the dining hall.
examples.zh: 我们在食堂的「共用长桌」旁找到了两个空位。

examples.en: A group from our class joined us at the communal table.
examples.zh: 我们班的几个同学也坐到了这张「共用长桌」旁边。

words.enDefinition: A tall chair allowing a small child to sit at table height

examples.en: We asked for a high chair when my friend brought her toddler.
examples.zh: 朋友带着她刚学会走路的孩子来了，我们就要了把「儿童餐椅」。

examples.en: The server moved an adult seat to make room for the high chair.
examples.zh: 服务员挪开一个成人座位，腾出地方放「儿童餐椅」。

words.enDefinition: To move from one restaurant table to another during a visit

examples.en: We asked to change tables because the speaker above us was loud.
examples.zh: 我们头顶的音响太响，就问能不能「换桌」。

examples.en: The host said we could change tables once the group beside us left.
examples.zh: 迎宾员说，等旁边一桌客人离开后我们可以「换桌」。

collocations: offer to let guests change tables

words.enDefinition: Words telling waiting diners they can now be shown to their table

examples.en: I got a text saying our table is ready while we waited outside.
examples.zh: 我们在外面等着时，我收到短信说「桌位已经准备好」。

examples.en: The host told us our table is ready while we looked at the menu.
examples.zh: 我们看菜单时，迎宾员说「桌位已经准备好」。

collocations: let us know the table is ready
send a text when the table is ready

words.enDefinition: Service in which staff take orders and bring food to diners' tables

examples.en: The café near campus offered table service only in the upstairs room.
examples.zh: 学校附近的咖啡馆只在楼上的用餐区提供「餐桌服务」。

examples.en: I asked whether the dining area had table service or a counter.
examples.zh: 我问用餐区是有「餐桌服务」还是需要到柜台去。

words.enDefinition: The number used to identify a particular table at a venue

examples.en: The server asked me for the table number printed on our sign.
examples.zh: 服务员让我报一下桌牌上印的「桌号」。

examples.en: I read out the table number so my friends could find us.
examples.zh: 我报了「桌号」，好让朋友找到我们。

words.enDefinition: A person who takes orders and serves food in a restaurant

examples.en: The server brought us a second menu when our friend arrived.
examples.zh: 朋友到了之后，「餐厅服务员」又给我们拿来一份菜单。

examples.en: I asked the server which of the dishes came with rice.
examples.zh: 我问「餐厅服务员」哪些菜配米饭。

words.enDefinition: A restaurant worker who carries finished dishes from kitchen to tables

examples.en: The food runner checked our table number before setting down two plates.
examples.zh: 「传菜员」核对了桌号，才把两个盘子放下。

examples.en: I told the food runner which person had ordered the soup.
examples.zh: 我告诉「传菜员」哪位客人点了汤。

collocations: a food runner from the kitchen

words.enDefinition: The room in a restaurant where customers sit and eat

examples.en: The dining room at the café was quieter than the front counter.
examples.zh: 这家咖啡馆的「餐厅用餐区」比前台安静。

examples.en: Our group waited near the entrance to the dining room after class.
examples.zh: 下课后，我们一行人在「餐厅用餐区」入口附近等人。

collocations: a table in the dining room
serve diners in the dining room

words.enDefinition: A list of dishes offered specifically during lunch service

examples.en: The café still had its lunch menu when we arrived after class.
examples.zh: 我们下课后到咖啡馆时，还能点「午餐菜单」上的菜。

examples.en: I showed my friend the lunch menu posted outside the entrance.
examples.zh: 我给朋友看了入口外贴着的「午餐菜单」。

words.enDefinition: A list of sweet dishes a restaurant serves after a meal

examples.en: We asked to see the dessert menu after finishing our main dishes.
examples.zh: 我们吃完主菜后，请服务员拿来「甜点菜单」。

examples.en: The dessert menu listed a cake my roommate wanted to try.
examples.zh: 「甜点菜单」上有一种我室友想尝的蛋糕。

words.enDefinition: A list of beverages offered in a restaurant or café

examples.en: I checked the drinks menu to see which teas they served.
examples.zh: 我查看了「饮品单」，想看看店里供应哪些茶。

examples.en: The server brought us a drinks menu before taking our food orders.
examples.zh: 服务员在给我们点菜前拿来了一份「饮品单」。

words.enDefinition: A selection of dishes and portions intended for young diners

examples.en: My friend asked for the children's menu when her son arrived.
examples.zh: 朋友的儿子到了之后，她要了一份「儿童菜单」。

examples.en: The children's menu had pictures beside the names of the dishes.
examples.zh: 「儿童菜单」的菜名旁印了图片。

words.enDefinition: A changing selection featuring ingredients available at a particular time of year

examples.en: The café posted its new seasonal menu beside the front door.
examples.zh: 咖啡馆在前门旁贴出了新的「时令菜单」。

examples.en: My flatmate chose a dish from the seasonal menu after class.
examples.zh: 我室友下课后从「时令菜单」上点了一道菜。

words.enDefinition: A dish offered in addition to the restaurant's regular choices that day

examples.en: The server told us about the daily special while we read the menu.
examples.zh: 我们看菜单时，服务员介绍了「当日特色菜」。

examples.en: I chose the daily special because I had never tried that dish.
examples.zh: 我选了「当日特色菜」，因为之前没吃过那道菜。

collocations: a board listing the daily special

words.enDefinition: A board showing dishes offered for a limited period

examples.en: The specials board was beside the counter near the main entrance.
examples.zh: 「特色菜牌」就在靠近正门的柜台旁。

examples.en: I read the specials board while my roommate found us a table.
examples.zh: 室友去找桌位的时候，我看了看「特色菜牌」。

words.enDefinition: The soup a restaurant is featuring on a particular day

examples.en: I asked what the soup of the day was before choosing my starter.
examples.zh: 选前菜之前，我问了「当日例汤」是什么。

examples.en: My friend ordered the soup of the day with a piece of bread.
examples.zh: 朋友点了「当日例汤」，配一片面包。

collocations: ask for the soup of the day
order the soup of the day
a bowl of the soup of the day

words.enDefinition: A dish a restaurant or chef is especially known for

examples.en: We shared the signature dish after the server recommended it to us.
examples.zh: 服务员推荐了「招牌菜」，我们就点了一份分着吃。

examples.en: The menu showed a photo of the restaurant's signature dish.
examples.zh: 菜单上印着这家餐厅「招牌菜」的照片。

words.enDefinition: A dish the chef suggests customers try on a menu

examples.en: The chef's recommendation appeared on a small card beside the regular menu.
examples.zh: 「主厨推荐菜」写在一张小卡片上，就放在常规菜单旁边。

examples.en: I tried the chef's recommendation when my classmates chose the same dish.
examples.zh: 同学都点了「主厨推荐菜」，我也点了一份尝尝。

collocations: a dish marked as the chef's recommendation

words.enDefinition: A small dish eaten before the main part of a meal

examples.en: We split one appetizer before our rice dishes came out.
examples.zh: 米饭套餐端上来之前，我们分吃了一道「餐前小菜」。

examples.en: The server asked whether we wanted an appetizer to share.
examples.zh: 服务员问我们要不要点一道「餐前小菜」一起吃。

words.enDefinition: The main dish in a meal on American restaurant menus

examples.en: The American menu listed a side dish with every entrée.
examples.zh: 这份美国菜单上的每道「主菜」都附一份配菜。

examples.en: Our server asked each person to choose an entrée before ordering dessert.
examples.zh: 服务员请每个人在点甜点前选一道「主菜」。

words.enDefinition: Small portions of prepared dishes served as part of a meal

examples.en: The café offered small plates for people wanting a lighter lunch.
examples.zh: 咖啡馆为想少吃一点的人提供「小份菜」。

examples.en: Our group ordered three small plates instead of one large dish each.
examples.zh: 我们一行点了三份「小份菜」，没有每人点一大份。

words.enDefinition: A large plate of food intended to be eaten by several people

examples.en: Three of us ordered a sharing platter of dips and bread.
examples.zh: 我们三个人点了一份有蘸酱和面包的「分享拼盘」。

examples.en: The server explained how many people the sharing platter would serve.
examples.zh: 服务员说明了这份「分享拼盘」够几个人吃。

words.enDefinition: A planned sequence of several small dishes served in one meal

examples.en: The tasting menu let us try small portions of several different dishes.
examples.zh: 点「品鉴菜单」，我们就能尝到几道不同的菜，每道都是小份。

examples.en: My classmate asked what the first course on the tasting menu was.
examples.zh: 同学问「品鉴菜单」里的第一道菜是什么。

words.enDefinition: A menu offering a defined selection of courses at one price

examples.en: We tried the set menu because there were several courses to share.
examples.zh: 我们点了「固定套餐菜单」上的餐，里面有好几道菜可以一起吃。

examples.en: The set menu offered two choices for each course of the meal.
examples.zh: 「固定套餐菜单」的每一道都能从两种菜里选。

words.enDefinition: Choosing separate dishes from a menu, with each priced individually

examples.en: The server asked whether we wanted to order à la carte for lunch.
examples.zh: 服务员问我们午饭想不想「按单道菜点」。

examples.en: We asked which dishes could be ordered à la carte that evening.
examples.zh: 我们问那天晚上有哪些菜可以「按单道菜点」。

words.enDefinition: A meal with three separately served parts, often including dessert

examples.en: The event ended with a three-course meal at a restaurant near campus.
examples.zh: 活动最后在学校附近的餐厅吃了一顿「三道式餐点」。

examples.en: We asked what the first part of the three-course meal would be.
examples.zh: 我们问「三道式餐点」的头一道会是什么。

words.enDefinition: One of the available meals that contains no meat or fish

examples.en: I asked whether there was a vegetarian option at the campus café.
examples.zh: 我问校园咖啡馆有没有「素食选项」。

examples.en: The vegetarian option came with the same two sides as my friend's meal.
examples.zh: 我点的「素食选项」和朋友的餐搭配了同样两份配菜。

collocations: a vegetarian option on the menu

words.enDefinition: An available meal or dish made without ingredients from animals

examples.en: The server showed me the vegan option on a separate page.
examples.zh: 服务员给我看了单独一页上的「纯素选项」。

examples.en: Our group chose the café after checking that it offered a vegan option.
examples.zh: 我们确认这家咖啡馆有「纯素选项」才选了这里。

words.enDefinition: A meal in which several items are offered together as one order

examples.en: The student café offered a combo meal with soup and a sandwich.
examples.zh: 学生咖啡馆提供一种含汤和三明治的「组合套餐」。

examples.en: I asked which drink came with the combo meal on the board.
examples.zh: 我问牌子上的「组合套餐」配哪种饮料。

collocations: a combo meal with a drink

words.enDefinition: A smaller dish that is part of the meal as listed

examples.en: The salad was an included side on the menu we saw online.
examples.zh: 我们在网上看的菜单上，沙拉是「随餐配菜」。

examples.en: I asked if rice was an included side for the fish.
examples.zh: 我问那道鱼有没有米饭当「随餐配菜」。

collocations: an included side with the meal

words.enDefinition: The amount of food provided in a particular restaurant order

examples.en: We asked about the portion size before ordering a plate to share.
examples.zh: 点一盘大家分之前，我们先问了「一份的分量」。

examples.en: The portion size was larger than I had expected from the photo.
examples.zh: 「一份的分量」比我看照片时想的要大。

words.enDefinition: An order containing about half the amount of a standard portion

examples.en: I asked whether the café offered a half portion of pasta.
examples.zh: 我问咖啡馆的意面能不能点「半份」。

examples.en: My friend ordered a half portion because she wanted dessert later.
examples.zh: 朋友想过会儿再吃甜点，所以只点了「半份」。

words.enDefinition: The usual amount of a dish served to one customer

examples.en: The server said a regular portion would be enough for one person.
examples.zh: 服务员说，一个人点「标准份」就够了。

examples.en: I ordered a regular portion of fries to go with my sandwich.
examples.zh: 我点了「标准份」的薯条配三明治。

words.enDefinition: A menu category for side dishes and additional ingredients

examples.en: The menu listed bread and extra dressing under sides and extras near the bottom.
examples.zh: 菜单接近底部的「配菜与加料」栏列出了面包和额外的酱汁。

examples.en: I checked the sides and extras section before choosing something for the table.
examples.zh: 给大家点东西之前，我先看了「配菜与加料」一栏。

collocations: a section for sides and extras

words.enDefinition: A salad dressing featured as the restaurant's own choice

examples.en: I asked what the house dressing tasted like before ordering my salad.
examples.zh: 选沙拉之前，我问了「店家招牌沙拉酱」是什么味道。

examples.en: The server poured the house dressing into a small dish for me.
examples.zh: 服务员把「店家招牌沙拉酱」倒进一个小碟子给了我。

words.enDefinition: A mixed drink resembling a cocktail without containing alcohol

examples.en: My friend ordered a mocktail with lime and mint for lunch.
examples.zh: 朋友午餐点了有青柠和薄荷的「无酒精调饮」。

examples.en: The drinks menu listed one mocktail made with ginger and apple.
examples.zh: 饮品单上有一款用姜和苹果做的「无酒精调饮」。

collocations: a mocktail on the drinks menu

words.enDefinition: A combination chosen so a drink complements a particular dish

examples.en: I asked the server about a food and drink pairing for the salty dishes.
examples.zh: 我问服务员偏咸的菜该怎么做「餐点饮品搭配」。

examples.en: The menu suggested a food and drink pairing with iced tea for the meal.
examples.zh: 菜单建议用冰茶做这顿饭的「餐点饮品搭配」。

collocations: suggest a food and drink pairing
try a food and drink pairing
a suggested food and drink pairing

words.enDefinition: To listen to and record what we want to eat

examples.en: The server came to take our order after our last friend arrived.
examples.zh: 最后一位朋友到场后，服务员过来「给我们点单」。

examples.en: We waited near the counter for someone to take our order at lunch.
examples.zh: 午饭时我们在柜台边等店员「给我们点单」。

collocations: come over to take our order
be ready to take our order
wait for someone to take our order

words.enDefinition: Having chosen what to request from a restaurant or café

examples.en: The server asked whether we were ready to order after bringing the drinks.
examples.zh: 服务员送来饮料后，问我们是否「准备好点单」。

examples.en: I was not ready to order because I had just arrived from class.
examples.zh: 我刚下课赶过来，还没「准备好点单」。

collocations: tell the server you're ready to order
wait until everyone is ready to order

words.zhGloss: 能再给我们一点时间吗
words.enDefinition: A polite request for longer to decide before ordering food
acceptedZhAnswers: 能再给我们一点时间吗

examples.en: When the server returned, I asked, "Could we have another minute?" and kept reading.
examples.zh: 服务员回来时，我问「能再给我们一点时间吗？」然后继续看菜单。

examples.en: I asked, "Could we have another minute?" because my friend was still choosing lunch.
examples.zh: 我问「能再给我们一点时间吗？」因为朋友还没选好午饭。

collocations: say "Could we have another minute to decide?"
ask "Could we have another minute, please?"

words.enDefinition: A question inviting a server to suggest a dish or drink

examples.en: I asked, "What do you recommend?" when the server described the lunch menu.
examples.zh: 服务员介绍午餐菜单时，我问「您推荐什么？」

examples.en: My roommate asked, "What do you recommend?" after finding three dishes she liked.
examples.zh: 室友看到三道都想尝的菜，就问「您推荐什么？」

collocations: say "What do you recommend for lunch?"
ask "What do you recommend with this dish?"

words.enDefinition: A question asking which items accompany a particular order

examples.en: I pointed at the fish and asked, "What comes with that?" before ordering.
examples.zh: 点菜前，我指着鱼问「这道菜配什么？」

examples.en: My friend asked, "What comes with that?" when the server mentioned the rice bowl.
examples.zh: 服务员提到那款盖饭时，朋友问「这道菜配什么？」

collocations: say "What comes with that main dish?"
ask "What comes with that, besides the salad?"

words.enDefinition: A phrase telling a server to repeat someone else's order

examples.en: After my roommate ordered the soup, I said, "I’ll have the same," and smiled.
examples.zh: 室友点了汤，我笑着说「我也要一样的。」

examples.en: I pointed to her plate and said, "I’ll have the same," to the server.
examples.zh: 我指着她的盘子跟服务员说「我也要一样的」。

collocations: order by saying "I'll have the same."

words.enDefinition: A phrase confirming your choice of the item just discussed

examples.en: The server described the soup, and I said, "I’ll go with that," right away.
examples.zh: 服务员介绍了那份汤，我当即说「我就选这个。」

examples.en: I read the description and told the server, "I’ll go with that," instead.
examples.zh: 看过说明后，我改口对服务员说「我就选这个。」

collocations: confirm with "I'll go with that, please."

words.enDefinition: A polite question asking to exchange the included side dish

examples.en: I asked, "Can I swap the side?" because I wanted rice with the fish.
examples.zh: 我想用米饭配鱼，就问「我可以换一道配菜吗？」

examples.en: My friend asked, "Can I swap the side?" when the server mentioned the fries.
examples.zh: 服务员说配薯条时，朋友问「我可以换一道配菜吗？」

collocations: say "Can I swap the side for rice?"
ask "Can I swap the side, please?"

words.enDefinition: To choose rice instead of the normally included fries

examples.en: The server said I could substitute rice for fries with the fish dish.
examples.zh: 服务员说，点鱼可以「用米饭换薯条」。

examples.en: I asked whether I could substitute rice for fries for my lunch order.
examples.zh: 我问午餐可不可以「用米饭换薯条」。

collocations: ask to substitute rice for fries
offer to substitute rice for fries
choose to substitute rice for fries

words.enDefinition: Dressing served separately rather than mixed into the salad

examples.en: I asked for dressing on the side so we could share the salad.
examples.zh: 我们打算分吃沙拉，我请服务员把「沙拉酱另外放」。

examples.en: The café brought dressing on the side in a small bowl beside my plate.
examples.zh: 咖啡馆把「沙拉酱另外放」，用小碗装着放在我盘子旁边。

collocations: ask for dressing on the side
order with dressing on the side

words.enDefinition: Sauce served in its own container apart from the main food

examples.en: I ordered the fish with sauce on the side for our shared lunch.
examples.zh: 我们一起吃午饭，我点了鱼，请店员把「酱汁另外放」。

examples.en: I asked whether the café always served sauce on the side with that dish.
examples.zh: 我问这家咖啡馆上这道菜时是不是总把「酱汁另外放」。

collocations: ask for sauce on the side
order with sauce on the side

words.enDefinition: To leave onions out of the food being ordered

examples.en: I asked the server to hold the onions on my sandwich.
examples.zh: 我请服务员在我的三明治里「不放洋葱」。

examples.en: My roommate wanted to hold the onions on one of our dishes.
examples.zh: 室友想请店员在我们的一道菜里「不放洋葱」。

collocations: a request to hold the onions

words.enDefinition: Additional pieces of cloth or paper for use while eating

examples.en: I asked for extra napkins after we ordered the sharing platter.
examples.zh: 我们点了分享拼盘后，我又要了「多几张餐巾」。

examples.en: The server left extra napkins on the table with the plates.
examples.zh: 服务员放下盘子，还给我们「多拿了几张餐巾」。

words.enDefinition: A request for a drink to be served without ice

examples.en: I asked for my iced tea with no ice this time.
examples.zh: 这次我请店员给我的冰茶「不加冰」。

examples.en: My roommate said "No ice, please" when the server brought water.
examples.zh: 服务员送来水时，室友说「不加冰」。

collocations: a glass of water with no ice

words.enDefinition: An added piece or amount of lemon served with an order

examples.en: I asked for extra lemon with the water at our table.
examples.zh: 我请店员给桌上的水「多加点柠檬」。

examples.en: The server offered extra lemon when she brought me the tea.
examples.zh: 服务员给我端来茶时，问要不要「多加点柠檬」。

words.enDefinition: Prepared with less salt than would normally be used

examples.en: My roommate asked for the fries light on the salt at lunch today.
examples.zh: 今天午饭时，室友请店员给薯条「少放点盐」。

examples.en: I told the server I preferred the soup light on the salt this time.
examples.zh: 我告诉服务员，这次希望汤里「少放点盐」。

collocations: ask for it light on the salt
serve it light on the salt

words.enDefinition: Having a moderate amount of heat from ingredients like chili

examples.en: My friend asked for something not too spicy while reading the lunch menu.
examples.zh: 朋友看午餐菜单时，问有没有「别太辣」的菜。

examples.en: I chose the noodles after the server said they were not too spicy.
examples.zh: 服务员说面条「不太辣」，我就点了它。

collocations: ask for it not too spicy

words.enDefinition: A question about the strength of a dish's chili heat

examples.en: I asked, "How spicy is it?" when my friend pointed out the noodle soup.
examples.zh: 朋友指着那碗汤面时，我问「这道菜有多辣？」

examples.en: My roommate said, "How spicy is it?" before deciding whether to try it.
examples.zh: 室友先问「这道菜有多辣？」再决定要不要尝。

collocations: say "How spicy is it compared with the curry?"
ask "How spicy is it without the sauce?"

words.enDefinition: To request food intended for everyone seated at the same table

examples.en: My classmates asked me to order for the table because I knew the menu.
examples.zh: 我熟悉菜单，同学便请我「给全桌人点」菜。

examples.en: We decided to order for the table after agreeing on three dishes to share.
examples.zh: 商量好分吃哪三道菜后，我们决定「给全桌人点」。

collocations: choose dishes to order for the table
ask who will order for the table

words.enDefinition: To request another set of drinks for the same group

examples.en: We stayed to talk and decided to order another round of tea.
examples.zh: 我们留下来聊天，决定「再点一轮」茶。

examples.en: My roommate asked if we could order another round before the café closed.
examples.zh: 室友问，咖啡馆关门之前能不能「再点一轮」。

words.enDefinition: To request an extra item with an order already made

examples.en: We asked to add to our order after our friends arrived at the table.
examples.zh: 朋友们入座后，我们请服务员「给我们加单」。

examples.en: My flatmate wanted to add to our order before the kitchen took its final orders.
examples.zh: 厨房停止接单前，室友想请店员「给我们加单」。

collocations: ask to add to our order
want to add to our order
call the server over to add to our order

words.enDefinition: An additional plate requested for someone at a dining table

examples.en: I asked for one more plate so our friend could share the food.
examples.zh: 我请服务员「再来一个盘子」，好让朋友也能分着吃。

examples.en: The server brought one more plate when the sharing dish arrived.
examples.zh: 服务员端来分享菜，还「拿来了一个盘子」。

words.enDefinition: Individual plates provided so diners can share food and eat separately

examples.en: We asked for separate plates to share the dessert more easily.
examples.zh: 我们要了「分开的盘子」，好分着吃甜点。

examples.en: The server brought two separate plates with the sharing platter.
examples.zh: 服务员端来分享拼盘，也给了我们两个「分开的盘子」。

words.enDefinition: To serve several dishes at roughly the same time

examples.en: We asked the server to bring the dishes out together because we were sharing everything.
examples.zh: 我们所有菜都分着吃，就请服务员「把菜一起端上来」。

examples.en: The café said it could bring the dishes out together once our friend arrived.
examples.zh: 咖啡馆说，等朋友到了就可以「把菜一起端上来」。

collocations: ask to bring the dishes out together
offer to bring the dishes out together
try to bring the dishes out together

words.enDefinition: To bring the opening dish before other parts of the meal

examples.en: We asked the server to serve the starter first while we chose our main dishes.
examples.zh: 我们点主菜时，请服务员「先上前菜」。

examples.en: The restaurant said it would serve the starter first and then bring the noodles.
examples.zh: 餐厅说会「先上前菜」，接着端上面条。

collocations: ask to serve the starter first
offer to serve the starter first
remember to serve the starter first

words.enDefinition: To pour more water into glasses that have partly emptied

examples.en: The server came over to top up our water halfway through our meal.
examples.zh: 我们吃到一半时，服务员过来「给我们续点水」。

examples.en: My flatmate asked if someone could top up our water before dessert.
examples.zh: 室友问甜点上来以前能不能请人「给我们续点水」。

collocations: offer to top up our water
ask someone to top up our water
come by to top up our water

words.enDefinition: To remove used plates from the table after people finish eating

examples.en: The server waited until we had finished to clear our plates.
examples.zh: 服务员等我们吃完才来「收走我们的盘子」。

examples.en: We asked if she could clear our plates to make room for dessert.
examples.zh: 为了给甜点腾出地方，我们请她「收走我们的盘子」。

collocations: ask someone to clear our plates

words.enDefinition: To find out whether an ordered dish is ready or pending

examples.en: The server offered to check on a dish that had not arrived yet.
examples.zh: 服务员主动提出帮我们「问一道菜好了没」，那道菜还未上桌。

examples.en: I asked whether someone could check on a dish for my friend.
examples.zh: 我问能否请人帮朋友「问一道菜好了没」。

collocations: ask the kitchen to check on a dish
offer to check on a dish
check on a dish that hasn’t arrived

words.expression: excuse me, we’re still waiting for
words.lemma: excuse me, we’re still waiting for
words.enDefinition: A polite lead-in for asking about an order that has not arrived
acceptedEnVariants: excuse me, we’re still waiting for

examples.en: I said, "Excuse me, we’re still waiting for the soup," when the server came back.
examples.zh: 服务员回来时，我说「不好意思，我们还在等那份汤」。

examples.en: My friend said, "Excuse me, we’re still waiting for our tea," while we finished lunch.
examples.zh: 午饭快吃完时，朋友说「不好意思，我们还在等那份茶」。

collocations: say "Excuse me, we're still waiting for our soup."
say "Excuse me, we're still waiting for the rice."
say "Excuse me, we're still waiting for one dish."

words.enDefinition: Any drink someone might want to order or be served

examples.en: The server asked if we wanted something to drink before choosing our meals.
examples.zh: 服务员问我们选餐之前要不要来「喝的东西」。

examples.en: My roommate ordered something to drink while waiting for two friends to arrive.
examples.zh: 室友等两位朋友来时，先点了「喝的东西」。

words.expression: I think this is for another table
words.lemma: i think this is for another table
words.enDefinition: A polite way to tell staff a dish belongs elsewhere
acceptedEnVariants: I think this is for another table

examples.en: I said, "I think this is for another table," when the server brought us noodles.
examples.zh: 服务员给我们端来面条时，我说「这应该是另一桌点的」。

examples.en: My roommate looked at the plate and said, "I think this is for another table."
examples.zh: 室友看了看盘子，说「这应该是另一桌点的」。

collocations: say "I think this is for another table."
tell the server "I think this is for another table."
politely say "I think this is for another table."

words.zhGloss: 不好意思我点的不是这个
words.enDefinition: A polite correction when your food is not what you requested
acceptedZhAnswers: 不好意思我点的不是这个

examples.en: I told the server, "Sorry, I ordered something different," when the burger arrived.
examples.zh: 汉堡端来时，我对服务员说「不好意思，我点的不是这个」。

examples.en: My friend said, "Sorry, I ordered something different." before pointing to the menu.
examples.zh: 朋友说「不好意思，我点的不是这个」，然后指了指菜单。

collocations: start with "Sorry, I ordered something different."

words.enDefinition: A dish included in the order that has not reached the table

examples.en: We asked about the missing dish after the other plates arrived.
examples.zh: 其他菜都上桌之后，我们问了那道「漏上的菜」。

examples.en: The server checked our order slip for the missing dish from lunch.
examples.zh: 服务员查看了午餐点菜单，确认那道「漏上的菜」。

words.enDefinition: A mistake in recording, preparing, or serving what someone ordered

examples.en: The server apologized for the order mix-up before bringing my soup.
examples.zh: 服务员先为「弄错点单」道了歉，然后端来我的汤。

examples.en: We noticed an order mix-up when two sandwiches came to our table.
examples.zh: 两份三明治端到桌上时，我们发现店里「弄错点单」了。

words.enDefinition: To ask staff to take back a dish with a problem

examples.en: I asked if I could send a dish back because it was the wrong order.
examples.zh: 上的不是我点的菜，我问能不能「把菜退回厨房」。

examples.en: My friend decided to send a dish back after speaking quietly with the server.
examples.zh: 朋友和服务员小声说过情况后，决定「把菜退回厨房」。

collocations: ask to send a dish back
decide to send a dish back
when to send a dish back

words.enDefinition: Another serving brought after the original dish was wrong or unsuitable

examples.en: The server offered a replacement dish after taking away the noodles.
examples.zh: 服务员端走面条后，提出可以给我们一份「替换上的菜」。

examples.en: Our replacement dish arrived just as the others finished their lunches.
examples.zh: 我们的「替换上的菜」端上来时，其他人刚吃完午饭。

words.zhGloss: 能帮我们核对一下点单吗
words.enDefinition: A polite request for staff to verify the restaurant order
acceptedZhAnswers: 能帮我们核对一下点单吗

examples.en: I asked, "Can you check our order?" when we received two bowls instead of three.
examples.zh: 我们点了三碗，只端来两碗时，我问「能帮我们核对一下点单吗？」

examples.en: My roommate said, "Can you check our order?" before the server left our table.
examples.zh: 服务员离开桌边前，室友问「能帮我们核对一下点单吗？」

collocations: say "Can you check our order, please?"
ask "Can you check our order for the soup?"

words.enDefinition: A statement explaining that an item was not requested by your group

examples.en: I said, "We didn’t order this," when a second salad arrived.
examples.zh: 又端来一份沙拉时，我说「这不是我们点的」。

examples.en: My friend said, "We didn’t order this," and pointed to the extra plate.
examples.zh: 朋友指着多出来的盘子说「这不是我们点的」。

collocations: tell the server "We didn't order this side dish."

words.enDefinition: A phrase saying a part of the order has not arrived

examples.en: My roommate said, "Something is missing." She checked the receipt again.
examples.zh: 室友说「少了一样东西」，又核对了一遍小票。

examples.en: At lunch I said, "Something is missing." We were waiting for the side.
examples.zh: 午饭时我说「少了一样东西」，我们还在等配菜。

collocations: say "Something is missing from our order."
explain "Something is missing from this meal."
tell the server "Something is missing from the tray."

words.enDefinition: A polite phrase used to request an item for a group

examples.en: I asked, "Could you bring us another spoon?" when our dessert arrived.
examples.zh: 甜点端上来时，我问「能给我们再拿把勺子吗？」

examples.en: My roommate said, "Could you bring us some napkins?" after the soup spilled.
examples.zh: 汤洒了之后，室友问「能给我们拿些餐巾吗？」

collocations: could you bring us another spoon
could you bring us some water
could you bring us the dessert menu

words.enDefinition: No longer having any remaining portions of a particular dish

examples.en: The server said they were out of that dish and suggested the soup.
examples.zh: 服务员说「那道菜售完了」，推荐我们点汤。

examples.en: The café was out of that dish by the time we reached the counter.
examples.zh: 我们走到柜台时，餐厅「那道菜售完了」。

collocations: say you're out of that dish
apologize for being out of that dish

words.enDefinition: The final time when customers can request food or drinks

examples.en: We arrived before last orders and still had time to choose.
examples.zh: 我们在「最后一轮点单」之前到了，还有时间选菜。

examples.en: The café announced last orders as our study group was leaving.
examples.zh: 学习小组准备离开时，咖啡馆提醒大家「最后一轮点单」了。

words.enDefinition: Words used to say food preparation has ended for the day

examples.en: The server said, "The kitchen is closed," but offered us drinks.
examples.zh: 服务员说「厨房停止接单了」，不过还可以给我们上饮料。

examples.en: The notice said, "The kitchen is closed," so we chose another café.
examples.zh: 告示上写着「厨房停止接单了」，我们就换了家咖啡馆。

collocations: a sign saying the kitchen is closed
be told the kitchen is closed
hear that the kitchen is closed

words.enDefinition: An American dining phrase signaling you want the restaurant bill

examples.en: We were ready for the check right after we finished sharing the dessert.
examples.zh: 我们分完甜点后就「可以结账了」。

examples.en: The server asked whether our group was ready for the check before clearing the plates.
examples.zh: 服务员收盘子之前问我们是不是「可以结账了」。

collocations: tell someone you're ready for the check
let the server know you're ready for the check

words.enDefinition: To settle what you owe at a designated restaurant counter

examples.en: I offered to pay at the counter while my friends packed their bags.
examples.zh: 朋友们收拾包时，我主动提出「到柜台结账」。

examples.en: The café asked us to pay at the counter on our way out.
examples.zh: 咖啡馆请我们出去时「到柜台结账」。

collocations: ask to pay at the counter
let guests pay at the counter
a sign asking guests to pay at the counter

words.enDefinition: To settle the amount you owe without leaving your table

examples.en: The server asked if we wanted to pay at the table after dessert.
examples.zh: 甜点吃完后，服务员问我们是否想「在桌边结账」。

examples.en: My flatmate was surprised that we could pay at the table at that café.
examples.zh: 室友没想到在那家咖啡馆可以「在桌边结账」。

collocations: ask to pay at the table
let guests pay at the table
offer to pay at the table

words.expression: there’s a mistake on the bill
words.lemma: there’s a mistake on the bill
words.enDefinition: A polite way to point out an error in a bill
acceptedEnVariants: there’s a mistake on the bill

examples.en: I said, "There’s a mistake on the bill." I pointed to the second soup on the list.
examples.zh: 我说「账单上有一处错误」，指了指单子上的第二份汤。

examples.en: My flatmate said, "There’s a mistake on the bill." The server then checked our order.
examples.zh: 室友说「账单上有一处错误」，服务员随后核对了点单。

collocations: say "There's a mistake on the bill."
explain "There's a mistake on the bill here."
tell the server "There's a mistake on the bill."

words.enDefinition: A restaurant bill changed to fix an error in the original

examples.en: The server brought a corrected bill after removing the extra dessert.
examples.zh: 服务员扣掉多算的甜点后，拿来一份「更正后的账单」。

examples.en: I checked the corrected bill while my friends waited by the door.
examples.zh: 朋友们在门边等我时，我核对了「更正后的账单」。

words.enDefinition: To remove a particular item or charge from a bill

examples.en: The server offered to take it off the bill after checking what we ordered.
examples.zh: 服务员核对了我们点的东西后，主动提出「从账单上划掉这项」。

examples.en: I asked if the manager could take it off the bill before we paid.
examples.zh: 我问经理能不能在付钱前「从账单上划掉这项」。

collocations: ask to take it off the bill
agree to take it off the bill
offer to take it off the bill

words.enDefinition: A university facility where students can eat meals on campus

examples.en: We met at the campus dining hall between our afternoon classes.
examples.zh: 我们在两节下午课之间到「校园食堂」碰面。

examples.en: The campus dining hall offered a separate line for soup and sandwiches.
examples.zh: 「校园食堂」给汤和三明治设了单独的排队通道。

collocations: eat at the campus dining hall
meet at the campus dining hall

words.enDefinition: A flat container for carrying dishes through a self-service dining area

examples.en: I picked up a cafeteria tray before joining the lunch line.
examples.zh: 进午餐队伍前，我拿了一个「食堂托盘」。

examples.en: My cafeteria tray held a bowl, a plate, and two cups.
examples.zh: 我的「食堂托盘」放着一只碗、一个盘子和两个杯子。

words.enDefinition: A line of diners waiting to be given food or serve themselves

examples.en: Our class joined the serving line together after the lecture ended.
examples.zh: 讲座结束后，我们班的同学一起加入了「排队打饭的队伍」。

examples.en: The serving line split into two queues near the hot dishes.
examples.zh: 到热菜附近时，「排队打饭的队伍」分成了两列。

words.enDefinition: A food counter where diners choose items for their own salad

examples.en: I stopped at the salad bar before choosing my main dish.
examples.zh: 选主菜前，我先去了「自助沙拉台」。

examples.en: The salad bar had two kinds of dressing beside the vegetables.
examples.zh: 「自助沙拉台」在蔬菜旁摆了两种沙拉酱。

words.enDefinition: A staffed or self-service counter offering hot prepared food

examples.en: My roommate waited at the hot food station for a bowl of rice.
examples.zh: 室友在「热食档口」等一碗米饭。

examples.en: The hot food station near the entrance served soup and baked potatoes.
examples.zh: 入口旁的「热食档口」供应汤和烤土豆。

collocations: line up at the hot food station
choose from the hot food station

words.enDefinition: A dining counter where staff prepare dishes for each individual order

examples.en: We chose the made-to-order station so we could select our sandwich fillings.
examples.zh: 为了自己选三明治的馅料，我们去了「现点现做档口」。

examples.en: The made-to-order station was open when I arrived after my lecture.
examples.zh: 我下课后赶到时，「现点现做档口」还在营业。

words.enDefinition: A meal where diners choose and serve their own food from displays

examples.en: The university held a self-service buffet for students arriving before term.
examples.zh: 学校为开学前到校的同学办了一场「自取式自助餐」。

examples.en: Our group chose the self-service buffet because everyone wanted different dishes.
examples.zh: 每个人想吃的菜都不同，所以我们选了「自取式自助餐」。

words.enDefinition: A buffet allowing diners to take repeated servings during the meal

examples.en: My flatmates picked an all-you-can-eat buffet for a meal after exams.
examples.zh: 室友们选了「不限次自助餐」，准备考完试一起吃。

examples.en: We asked whether the all-you-can-eat buffet included the nearby dessert counter.
examples.zh: 我们问「不限次自助餐」包不包括旁边的甜点柜台。

words.enDefinition: One meal redeemed from a campus dining plan using an account

examples.en: I used a meal swipe before heading to my evening seminar.
examples.zh: 去参加晚上的研讨课之前，我用了一次「食堂刷卡餐次」。

examples.en: My roommate asked whether a meal swipe included the salad bar.
examples.zh: 室友问一次「食堂刷卡餐次」包不包括自助沙拉台。

words.enDefinition: A university arrangement giving students meals or funds for campus dining

examples.en: I checked whether my dining plan covered breakfast during the break.
examples.zh: 我查了「校园用餐计划」在假期里是否包含早餐。

examples.en: My roommate changed her dining plan at the start of term.
examples.zh: 室友在学期开始时换了「校园用餐计划」。

words.enDefinition: The place for leaving used trays after eating in a dining hall

examples.en: We left our bowls and plates at the tray return after lunch.
examples.zh: 午饭后，我们把碗和盘子放在「托盘回收处」。

examples.en: The tray return was near the door leading back to the library.
examples.zh: 「托盘回收处」就在通往图书馆的那扇门旁边。

collocations: leave dishes at the tray return

words.enDefinition: To take the food or drink you want without waiting for staff

examples.en: The sign said "Serve yourself," with the plates on a table nearby.
examples.zh: 牌子上写着「请自取」，餐盘放在旁边的桌上。

examples.en: I asked what "Serve yourself" meant on the sign by the drinks.
examples.zh: 我问饮品旁的牌子写的「请自取」是什么意思。

collocations: a sign saying to serve yourself

words.enDefinition: Drinking water requested for everyone seated at a table

examples.en: The server brought water for the table before we opened our menus.
examples.zh: 我们还没打开菜单，服务员就拿来了「给一桌人喝的水」。

examples.en: I asked for water for the table when the last two friends arrived.
examples.zh: 最后两位朋友到场时，我请服务员拿来「给一桌人喝的水」。

collocations: ask for water for the table

words.enDefinition: A basket used to serve bread at a dining table

examples.en: The server placed the bread basket in the middle of the table.
examples.zh: 服务员把「盛面包的篮子」放在桌子中央。

examples.en: My roommate passed me the bread basket after we ordered soup.
examples.zh: 我们点过汤后，室友把「盛面包的篮子」递给了我。

words.enDefinition: To request food at a service counter rather than from a table

examples.en: The sign said to order at the counter before finding a table upstairs.
examples.zh: 牌子上说，先「到柜台点单」，再上楼找座位。

examples.en: My friend asked whether we should order at the counter or wait for a server.
examples.zh: 朋友问我们是该「到柜台点单」，还是等服务员过来。

collocations: ask guests to order at the counter
tell people to order at the counter
need to order at the counter

words.enDefinition: A question offering to add something to a customer's order

examples.en: The server asked, "Anything else for you?" after taking our lunch orders.
examples.zh: 服务员记下午餐的点单后问「您还需要点什么吗？」

examples.en: After hearing "Anything else for you?" I ordered some bread for the table.
examples.zh: 听到「您还需要点什么吗？」我给全桌人又点了些面包。

collocations: finish taking an order with "Anything else for you?"

words.enDefinition: To avoid getting too full to enjoy something sweet afterward

examples.en: My roommate picked a small dish to leave room for dessert after lunch.
examples.zh: 室友点了一份小菜，要「留点肚子吃甜点」。

examples.en: We decided to share the pasta so we could leave room for dessert.
examples.zh: 我们决定分着吃意面，好「留点肚子吃甜点」。

collocations: try to leave room for dessert
want to leave room for dessert
remember to leave room for dessert
